names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 august, «Sfântul Ierarh Fabian, episcopul Romei», with the rank word left off.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Αυγούστου, «Άγιος Φάβιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Ρώμης», with the rank word and the see left off. The page's own text calls the form a mistake and gives Φαβιανός as the correct one, «ή σωστότερα Φαβιανός», so both stand in this note and the listing's form is the one recorded.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue’s second heading for the Julian 5 August, „Свешт. муч. Фавије (Фавијан) папа Римски.“ — Свешт. муч. left off, which §5 maps to `hieromartyr`, and папа Римски left off too, which §5 sends to `office` and which this folder already carries as «Bishop of Rome». **The heading prints a second spelling in brackets, (Фавијан), and the body uses both**; §6 allows one form per folder, so the headword before the bracket is stored and the gloss inside it is recorded here rather than added as a second form. `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports that either spelling folds with nothing.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «Prigoana a reînceput sub împăratul Decius, când, în anul 250, Sfântul Fabian, Episcopul Romei, și-a dat viața pentru Hristos, primind cununa muceniciei.»

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 august — «Sfântul Ierarh Fabian, episcopul Romei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Αυγούστου — «Άγιος Φάβιος ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Ρώμης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the listing's words are the folder's own reading: hieromartyr, bishop of Rome. The page then argues with its own day, and that is worth recording rather than resolving. It corrects the name — «Ο Άγιος Φάβιος (ή σωστότερα Φαβιανός) μαρτύρησε δια ξίφους», Fabius, or more correctly Fabianus, was martyred by the sword — and adds: «Στους καταλόγους των πάπων μεταξύ των μαρτύρων συγκαταλέγεται ο πάπας Φαβιανός (236 - 350 m.X.), που μαρτύρησαν επί Δεκίου την 20ή Ιανουαρίου (Ευσεβίου Εκκλ. Ιστορία κεφ. κθ')» — in the lists of the popes, pope Fabianus is counted among the martyrs, martyred under Decius on 20 January, citing Eusebius. The second of the page's two years is plainly a slip for 250, since the folder's `dates` already hold the death at 250 under Decius out of doxologia. So saint.gr keeps him on 5 August while naming 20 January as the day of the papal lists; one row per church is the schema, so the row is the day page read and the January reading is this note, and the question of whether the Greek 5 August and the Roman 20 January are one commemoration is in the report. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints no apolytikion and no kontakion, so no hymn is added.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.08.2026 (5. август ст. ст.) — „Свешт. муч. Фавије (Фавијан) папа Римски.“

attestations.note: The day’s second of four entries, and the Romanian and Greek both keep him on this same 5/8. His row was `undocumented`. **THE HEADING PRINTS TWO SPELLINGS OF HIS NAME AND ONE FORM IS STORED.** „Свешт. муч. Фавије (Фавијан) папа Римски.“ gives Фавије and then (Фавијан) in brackets, and the body uses both: „Најпре беше Фавијан сеоски свештеник, а по том, када при избору папе сиђе бео голуб на њега, изабран за папу.“ writes Фавијан and „Но кад се зацари опаки Декије, наста страшно гоњење хришћана, у коме пострада и св. Фавије, мачем обезглављен 250. год.“ writes Фавије. §6 allows one `sr` form per folder, so the headword is stored and the bracketed variant is recorded in the form’s own note rather than added as a second form; the choice is the reading that the word before the bracket is the book’s lemma and the word inside it the book’s gloss. **AUTHOR: a ruling would settle this for the rest of the wave, since the Prologue does this more than once.** **`dates` UNTOUCHED AND EXACTLY CORROBORATED.** The folder holds `death` 250, flat and `attested`, from doxologia; „Но кад се зацари опаки Декије, наста страшно гоњење хришћана, у коме пострада и св. Фавије, мачем обезглављен 250. год.“ gives the same 250 and adds the manner, beheaded with the sword when the wicked Decius came to the throne. A third source agreeing to the year is not a reason to touch it. **`types` AND `office` UNTOUCHED.** Свешт. муч. is `hieromartyr`, which the folder has; папа Римски is a see and §5 sends it to `office`, where this folder already carries «Bishop of Rome» and `bishop` beside it, so nothing is added and nothing is renamed — «Pope of Rome» is not in the four locale packs and an `office` that is not in all four is a defect. сеоски свештеник, a village priest, would give `presbyter` and is in the body, and is refused as a body word. **ONE `related` ROW WRITTEN, AND IT IS THIS FOLDER’S FIRST OF ANY KIND.** „Крсти цара Филипа и сина му царевића Филипа, и, уз помоћ крштеног сенатора Понтија, сруши многе идоле и идолске храмове.“ has him baptise the emperor Philip and his son, and with the help of the baptised senator Понтије throw down many idols and idol temples; „Много штићаше и помагаше цркву као сенатор, и би велики пријатељ папе Фавија.“, in the entry two below, has that senator protect and help the church and be a great friend of pope Фавије. **The two entries name each other**, which is as plain a relation as this book gives, and `pontius-the-senator` is created on this same day out of entry 3, so the row is written in both directions. The emperor Philip and his son hold no folder and take nothing; Decius is an emperor named to date a persecution. **NO `locations`:** Rome is named in a clause and the folder has never had the key. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person.
